item: A stall record lists a statement longer than the request that ended inside it, as evidence only (R206)
summary: The slow-statement rule keeps a row only if it ended inside the request and was not longer than it, which is right for the share (a 56.9 s SAVEPOINT read as 1.023 of a 55.6 s request) but drops the one shape a lock holder has: begun before the request, ended inside it. Reproduced through the real slowquery listeners and note_stall on a SQLite busy-wait (holder 6,001 ms, request 4,541 ms): the record named the waiter's own INSERT (share 0.999) and the holder was absent with no trace (/mnt/project-files/audit-0.5.0/inputs/stall-forensics-item-g.md). The statement evidence now carries began_before (the longest two such rows, each duration_ms, sql to 80 characters, began_before_s, overlap_share clamped to 1) beside the unchanged keys, absent when empty so a record without one costs nothing; found, share_of_request and classify are untouched, and the report's method text says the log has no thread id so a holder and a bystander look the same. The 174 s case stays empty. RC2 measured the cost (R210): +156 B once for the method sentence, +0 B without the key, +174 B with one entry and +332 B with two at field widths, and a full ring of two-entry records shows 105 of 200 against today's 128 (one entry each: 115), the member at most 199,216 B of 200,000; sql is clipped to 80 characters before JSON escaping, so a quote-heavy statement can serialise up to 160 B per entry. A larger record means fewer records shown, said in selection.shown / of, never bytes over the line.
